citation: Grgic J, Trexler ET, Lazinica B, Pedisic Z. Effects of caffeine intake on muscle strength and power: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2018;15:11.
population: Mostly young men, trained and untrained
result_effect_uncertainty: Strength SMD 0.20 (95% CI 0.03-0.36); power SMD 0.17 (0.00-0.34); upper body SMD 0.21 (0.02-0.39); lower body SMD 0.15 (-0.05 to 0.34); I2=0%
limitations_coi: Only 3 studies checked blinding (33-60% guessed correctly); mostly men; no industry funding listed
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC5839013); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Grgic J, Grgic I, Pickering C, Schoenfeld BJ, Bishop DJ, Pedisic Z. Wake up and smell the coffee: caffeine supplementation and exercise performance - an umbrella review of 21 published meta-analyses. Br J Sports Med. 2020;54(11):681-688.
outcome_measure: Endurance, strength, muscular endurance, power, jumping, speed
result_effect_uncertainty: Ergogenic across outcomes; moderate-quality evidence (GRADE) for muscle endurance, strength, anaerobic power, aerobic endurance; prediction intervals not always excluding zero; effects larger for aerobic than anaerobic. Pooled numbers not extracted (full text blocked)
limitations_coi: Overlap of primary studies across meta-analyses; mostly young men
verification: PubMed abstract; full-text PDF hosts blocked by proxy; OpenAlex is_retracted=false; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Bilondi HT, Valipour H, Khoshro S, Jamilian P, Ostadrahimi A, Zarezadeh M. The effect of caffeine supplementation on muscular strength and endurance: a meta-analysis of meta-analyses. Heliyon. 2024;10(15):e35025.
design: Umbrella meta-analysis (9 meta-analyses; AMSTAR2: 5 high, 4 moderate)
result_effect_uncertainty: Strength SMD 0.18 (95% CI 0.14-0.21); endurance SMD 0.30 (0.21-0.38)
limitations_coi: Re-pools overlapping meta-analyses, so CIs overstate precision; corrigendum exists (10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e40064) whose PMC text references an unrelated article, so its content is unclear
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC11336343); corrigendum located; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Xiao Y, Ding L, Xu Z, Liu J, Guo L, Barnes MJ, et al. Effects of acute caffeine intake on muscular power during resistance exercise: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Front Nutr. 2025;12:1686283.
result_effect_uncertainty: Velocity SMD 0.42 (0.19-0.65), I2 85%; power SMD 0.21 (0.12-0.30), I2 14%; habitual <3 mg/kg/d SMD 0.87 (0.72-1.02) vs >=3 mg/kg/d SMD 0.21; dose subgroups low 0.43, moderate 0.31, high 0.78 (no significant difference between doses)
limitations_coi: High heterogeneity for velocity; reported CI for high-habitual subgroup (0.11-1.02) looks like a typo; small n
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC12537405); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Grgic J. Exploring the minimum ergogenic dose of caffeine on resistance exercise performance: a meta-analytic approach. Nutrition. 2022;97:111604.
result_effect_uncertainty: Strength d 0.17 (0.03-0.31); endurance d 0.21 (0.07-0.35); mean velocity d 0.56 (0.12-1.01); similar to higher-dose effects
limitations_coi: Single-author review; few studies per outcome
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Pallares JG, Fernandez-Elias VE, Ortega JF, Munoz G, et al. Neuromuscular responses to incremental caffeine doses: performance and side effects. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2013;45(11):2184-2192.
outcome_measure: Bar velocity and power in squat and bench at 25-90% 1RM; cycling peak power; side effects
result_effect_uncertainty: 3 mg/kg raised velocity at 25-50% 1RM (+5.4-8.5% for all doses); 9 mg/kg needed for bench velocity and squat power at 90% 1RM; side effects 15-62% at 9 mg/kg
limitations_coi: Small n; no CIs in abstract
verification: PubMed and Europe PMC abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Guest NS, VanDusseldorp TA, Nelson MT, Grgic J, Schoenfeld BJ, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2021;18:1.
result_effect_uncertainty: 3-6 mg/kg consistently ergogenic; minimal effective dose may be as low as 2 mg/kg; about 9 mg/kg gives high side-effect incidence and is not required; usual timing 60 min before exercise
limitations_coi: COI: lead author consults for Nutrigenomix (genetic testing); 2 authors on Dymatize advisory board; one author has coffee-company consulting and a patent; ISSN has received grants from caffeine-product companies
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC7777221), including COI section; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Gardiner C, Weakley J, Burke LM, Roach GD, Sargent C, Maniar N, Townshend A, Halson SL. The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev. 2023;69:101764.
result_effect_uncertainty: Total sleep time -45 min; sleep efficiency -7%; sleep onset latency +9 min; WASO +12 min; N3/N4 deep sleep -11.4 min; modelled cut-offs: coffee (107 mg) >=8.8 h and pre-workout (217.5 mg) >=13.2 h before bed
limitations_coi: CIs not in abstract; cut-offs are meta-regression extrapolations, not directly tested
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Kocak A, Georgousopoulou E, Knight-Agarwal CR, Matthews R, et al. The effect of consuming caffeine before late afternoon/evening training or competition on sleep: a systematic review with meta-analysis. Sports (Basel). 2025;13(9):317.
design: Systematic review with meta-analysis (RCTs and quasi-experimental)
intervention_comparison: 3-6 mg/kg before late-afternoon or evening training vs placebo
outcome_measure: Sleep efficiency; total sleep time; subjective sleep
result_effect_uncertainty: Sleep efficiency MD -4.87% (95% CI -7.45 to -2.29), not robust to leave-one-out; total sleep time -32.5 min (-69.9 to +5.0), not significant; consistent subjective impairment
limitations_coi: Few small studies; mostly male; funded by Australian Government RTP scholarship; no COI
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC12473705); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Drake C, Roehrs T, Shambroom J, Roth T. Caffeine effects on sleep taken 0, 3, or 6 hours before going to bed. J Clin Sleep Med. 2013;9(11):1195-1200.
intervention_comparison: 400 mg at 0, 3, 6 h before bed vs placebo
result_effect_uncertainty: Significant sleep disturbance at all three timings including 6 h before bed (p<0.05); authors: 6 h before bed still has important disruptive effects
limitations_coi: Single high dose; small sample; effect magnitudes not extracted
verification: PubMed abstract (PMC body text not returned by API); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Lara B, Ruiz-Moreno C, Salinero JJ, Del Coso J. Time course of tolerance to the performance benefits of caffeine. PLoS One. 2019;14(1):e0210275.
result_effect_uncertainty: Peak power about +4.0 +/- 1.3% for first 15 days, then faded; Wingate +4.9 +/- 0.9% on days 1, 4, 15, 18; effect largest on day 1 and progressively smaller
limitations_coi: Cycling not lifting; n=11; no competing interests
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC6343867); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Grgic J, Mikulic P. Acute effects of caffeine supplementation on resistance exercise, jumping, and Wingate performance: no influence of habitual caffeine intake. Eur J Sport Sci. 2021;21(8):1165-1175.
population: Resistance-trained men (13 low users ~65 mg/d; 11 moderate-high users ~235 mg/d)
outcome_measure: Bench velocity, power, reps; CMJ; Wingate
result_effect_uncertainty: ES favouring caffeine 0.14-0.97; bench velocity +0.02-0.08 m/s; power +42-156 W; +1.2 reps; no group x condition interaction; r habitual vs change -0.29 to 0.32 (ns)
limitations_coi: Few very-high users (>400 mg/d); small subgroups
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Wilk M, Filip A, Krzysztofik M, Maszczyk A, Zajac A. The acute effect of various doses of caffeine on power output and velocity during the bench press exercise among athletes habitually using caffeine. Nutrients. 2019;11(7):1465.
population: Strength-trained men habitually using ~426 mg/d (5.2 mg/kg)
outcome_measure: Bench press 3x5 at 50% 1RM: power and velocity
result_effect_uncertainty: No significant differences at any dose; large ES only for 6-9 mg/kg in some sets
limitations_coi: Small n; light load only; authors declare no COI
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Filip-Stachnik A, Krzysztofik M, Del Coso J, Palka T, et al. The effect of acute caffeine intake on resistance training volume, prooxidant-antioxidant balance and muscle damage markers following a session of full-body resistance exercise in resistance-trained men habituated to caffeine. J Sports Sci Med. 2023 (volume/pages not verified).
outcome_measure: Total reps to failure in a full-body session; TUT; RPE; damage markers
result_effect_uncertainty: Total reps 185 +/- 14 vs 180 +/- 15 (p=0.276, ES 0.34); TUT 766 vs 757 s (ns); RPE ns
limitations_coi: n=10; underpowered for small effects
verification: PubMed and Europe PMC abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Barreto G, Esteves GP, Marticorena F, Oliveira TN, Grgic J, et al. Caffeine, CYP1A2 genotype, and exercise performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2024;56(2):328-339.
n: 13 studies; 440 participants (233 AA, 175 AC, 34 CC); 119 outcomes
intervention_comparison: Caffeine vs placebo by CYP1A2 rs762551 genotype
result_effect_uncertainty: AA SMD 0.30 (0.21-0.39); AC SMD 0.16 (0.06-0.25); CC SMD -0.22 (-0.44 to -0.01); CC effect improved with dose (+0.19 per mg/kg) and later exercise onset; no baseline imbalance in placebo values
limitations_coi: Only 34 CC; studies with reported COI influenced CC estimate; mixed outcomes
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Giraldez-Costas V, Ruiz-Moreno C, Gonzalez-Garcia J, Lara B, et al. Pre-exercise caffeine intake enhances bench press strength training adaptations. Front Nutr. 2021;8:622564.
intervention_comparison: 3 mg/kg caffeine vs placebo before each bench session; tested without capsule
result_effect_uncertainty: 1RM +13.5 +/- 7.8% vs +11.3 +/- 5.3% (p=0.53, no difference); velocity improved across more loads with caffeine (e.g. 100% 1RM 0.14 to 0.25 m/s)
limitations_coi: Very small, short; no hypertrophy measure; title overstates the finding; no commercial COI
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC7870503); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Pakulak A, Candow DG, Totosy de Zepetnek J, Forbes SC, Basta D. Effects of creatine and caffeine supplementation during resistance training on body composition, strength, endurance, rating of perceived exertion and fatigue in trained young adults. J Diet Suppl. 2022;19(5):587-602.
intervention_comparison: 3 mg/kg/d caffeine; creatine 0.1 g/kg/d; combined; placebo, 1 h before RT
outcome_measure: Ultrasound muscle thickness; FFM (BodPod); 1RM; reps at 50% 1RM
result_effect_uncertainty: No caffeine effect on any outcome; only creatine increased knee-extensor thickness (interaction p=0.049)
limitations_coi: Very small arms (n=6), badly underpowered; funding not checked
verification: PubMed abstract; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Ormsbee MJ, Mandler WK, Thomas DD, Ward EG, Kinsey AW, Simonavice E, Panton LB, Kim JS. The effects of six weeks of supplementation with multi-ingredient performance supplements and resistance training on anabolic hormones, body composition, strength, and power in resistance-trained men. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2012;9:49.
intervention_comparison: NO-Shotgun pre-workout plus NO-Synthesize post-workout (whey, casein, BCAA, creatine, beta-alanine, caffeine) vs isocaloric maltodextrin
result_effect_uncertainty: Lean mass 62.9 to 65.7 kg (MIPS) vs 63.5 to 64.8 kg (PLA), interaction p=0.017; 1RM gains similar; peak power up in MIPS only
limitations_coi: INDUSTRY FUNDED: independent research grant and product donation from Vital Pharmaceuticals (manufacturer); protein- and creatine-confounded vs carbohydrate placebo; small n
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC3542109), including funding statement; DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Nelson A, Camic CL, Foster C, Zajac B, Hoecherl K, Erickson JL, et al. Supplementation with a multi-ingredient pre-workout supplement does not augment resistance training adaptations in females. Int J Exerc Sci. 2019 (volume/pages not verified).
intervention_comparison: MusclePharm FitMiss Ignite pre-workout daily vs manufacturer-prepared placebo, plus RT
result_effect_uncertainty: No group x time differences in FFM (p=0.87), fat mass, or upper/lower 1RM gains (p=0.74, 0.53); no adverse change in BP, HR or lipids
limitations_coi: Manufacturer supplied product and placebo; small n; high dropout (29 recruited)
verification: Full text via Europe PMC (PMC6355134); DOI resolved via Crossref API 2026-11-15; no retraction/update flag

citation: Cohen PA, Travis JC, Vanhee C, Ohana D, Venhuis BJ. Nine prohibited stimulants found in sports and weight loss supplements: deterenol, phenpromethamine (Vonedrine), oxilofrine, octodrine, BMPEA, 1,3-DMAA, 1,4-DMAA, 1,3-DMBA and higenamine. Clin Toxicol (Phila). 2021;59(11):975-981.
design: Product analysis (3 independent labs: NSF, RIVM, Sciensano)
population: US sports and weight-loss supplements labelled as containing deterenol
result_effect_uncertainty: 9 prohibited stimulants detected, including octodrine (DMHA), 1,3-DMAA, BMPEA, higenamine; 8 different mixtures; up to 4 experimental stimulants per product; never tested in humans
limitations_coi: Sample targeted at products already listing deterenol, so not representative of all pre-workouts; US market; publisher correction 2022 (10.1080/15563650.2022.2027083), content not checked. Quantities deliberately not reproduced here (safety rule)
verification: PubMed and Europe PMC abstract; Crossref shows correction record
